title: HD 44892: the youngest (or oldest?) gas-harbouring debris disc around an intermediate-mass star
question: Whether gas and millimeter continuum dust emission are present around the 2.1 Myr hybrid debris disc candidate HD 44892, what their masses and origins (primordial vs. secondary) are, and whether the young 2.1 Myr or alternative 800 Myr age is favored.

data.angular_resolution: 0.44'' x 0.38'' (84 au x 72 au, PA -70.7 deg) for continuum; 0.46'' x 0.40'' (88 au x 76 au, PA -80.6 deg) for 12CO

what.value: Stellar parameters (temperature 7500 ± 500 K, luminosity 60.0 ± 20.0 L_odot, stellar mass 2.87 +0.67/-0.41 M_odot, age 2.1 +1.2/-1.0 Myr) and fractional IR excess at 12 um (7.86 +0.11/-2.27) of HD 44892

evidence.quote: HD 44892 has a temperature of 7500 ± 500K, a luminosity of 60.0 ± 20.0 $L_{\odot}$, stellar mass of 2.87 $^{+0.67}_{-0.41}$ $M_{\odot}$, and an age of 2.1 $^{+1.2}_{-1.0}$ Myr (cite: Iglesias2023X-shooterEvolution).
HD 44892 has a fractional IR excess at 12 $\mu$m of 7.86 $^{+0.11}_{-2.27}$ (cite: Iglesias2023X-shooterEvolution)

what.value: Radial velocity of HD 44892 (20.9 ± 0.6 km s^-1)

evidence.quote: (cite: Gontcharov2006PulkovoSystem) have calculated the radial velocity of the star to be 20.9 ± 0.6 km s$^{-1}$, which is the value adopted in this study.

what.value: Continuum and 12CO fluxes for NO Lup

evidence.loc: HD 44892 in the context of known gas-harbouring debris discs
evidence.quote: For NO Lup, using continuum and $^{12}$CO fluxes from (cite: Lovell2021ALMADispersal), we derive the CO gas mass, assuming gas temperature of 50 K, of (5.03 ± 1.13) $\times$ 10$^{-5}$ $M_{\oplus}$.

what.value: Data for Fomalhaut dust and CO gas mass derivation

evidence.loc: HD 44892 in the context of known gas-harbouring debris discs
evidence.quote: For Fomalhaut, using data from (cite: Matra2017DetectionComets) and (cite: MacGregor2017ADisk), we derive a 50 K dust mass of $(1.49\pm0.38)\times10^{-2}$$M_{\oplus}$ and a CO gas mass of $(1.89\pm0.55)\times10^{-7}$$M_{\oplus}$.

what.value: Data for eta Crv dust and CO gas mass derivation

evidence.loc: HD 44892 in the context of known gas-harbouring debris discs
evidence.quote: For $\eta$ Crv we derive a dust mass at 50 K of $(1.07\pm0.87)\times10^{-2}$$M_{\oplus}$ and a CO gas mass of $(5.92\pm0.78)\times10^{-7}$$M_{\oplus}$ (cite: Marino2017ALMAPlanets).

recipe.goal: Image continuum and measure flux and size
recipe.method: Image continuum with CASA tclean (Briggs weighting, robust=0.3), measure flux inside the 3-sigma contour, fit Gaussian component with CASA imfit, and verify astrometric accuracy.

recipe.goal: Subtract continuum, image CO lines, and extract moment maps and spectra
recipe.method: Subtract continuum with uvcontsub, identify emission channels with plotms, image CO SPWs with tclean (robust=0.3, then nchan=3 binning, then with Keplerian Mask tool), and create moment 0 maps with immoments over -8.49 to 15.33 km s^-1.
key_parameters: Velocity / frequency integration range: -8.49 to 15.33 km s^-1 (230.5445 GHz to 230.5262 GHz)
Keplerian mask parameters: inclination = 40 deg, PA = 17.2 deg, stellar mass = 3.27 M_odot, outer radius = 0.4'' (76 au)
assumptions: Star radial velocity in LSR frame ~1.5 km s^-1 (heliocentric 20.9 ± 0.6 km s^-1); Keplerian rotation around star

recipe.goal: Simulate dust ring models to constrain belt radius, dust temperature, dust mass, and collisional lifetime
recipe.method: Generate circular dust ring models (radii 20-100 au, width 1 px / 0.2 au) at various inclinations, simulate ALMA observations with CASA simalma, compare to data with imfit to find best-fit radius, compute blackbody temperature and optically thin dust mass, and estimate collisional lifetime.
key_parameters: Ring radii = 20-100 au; ring width = 1 px (0.2 au)
assumptions: Blackbody dust grains; optically thin thermal emission; distance D = 191 pc; stellar luminosity L = 60.0 L_odot; dust opacity kappa = 0.1 * 2.3 * (nu / 230e9)^0.7 cm^2 g^-1 (Beckwith 1990)

recipe.goal: Derive CO and total H2 gas masses and upper limits
recipe.method: Calculate minimum CO gas mass from 12CO (2-1) integrated flux assuming LTE and optically thin emission at 20 K and 50 K; derive 3-sigma upper limits from 13CO and C18O moment 0 RMS inside the 3-sigma 12CO contour; convert to total H2 mass assuming ISM abundance ratios.
key_parameters: Gas temperatures = 20 K and 50 K; 13CO and C18O 3-sigma flux upper limit = 90.84 mJy km s^-1
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE); Boltzmann level population; ISM abundance ratios 12CO/H2 = 10^-4, CO/13CO = 77, CO/C18O = 550

recipe.goal: Analyze optical UVES spectra for circumstellar absorption and mass accretion rate
recipe.method: Reduce UVES spectra with EsoReflex, correct telluric contamination with Molecfit, fit Kurucz stellar model spectra to identify Ca II K & H and Na I D1 & D2 absorption and residual variability, and compute mass accretion rate from H-alpha following Fairlamb et al. (2017).

recipe.goal: Model the spectral energy distribution (SED) and compare Spitzer IRS spectra
recipe.method: Fit single-temperature blackbody belt model to the infrared excess for stellar temperatures of 7000 K, 7500 K, and 8000 K (excluding IRAS 100 um upper limit), and compare Spitzer IRS mid-IR spectrum to reference protoplanetary and debris discs.
key_parameters: Stellar effective temperatures T_eff = 7000 K, 7500 K, 8000 K
assumptions: Optically thin dust; single-temperature blackbody belt

answer_key.quantity: Minimum dust mass (at 50 K)

answer_key.quantity: Collisional dust lifetime

evidence.quote: In this scenario, following (cite: Pearce2021Fomalhaut) (cite: Wyatt2002Collisions) we obtain the dust lifetime of order $10^{-2}$ Myr, which is much smaller than the estimated age of HD 44892.
